side_b: Direct provider APIs are simpler and better than a gateway hop.
reason: B conceded that a single direct client misses cross-vendor fallback.

turns.speaker: caesar
turns.text: A 2 – B 0. Latest: B. grounding=0.90. B conceded that a single direct client misses cross-vendor fallback.

topic: In a screening test with 99% sensitivity, 99% specificity, and 1% disease prevalence, does a positive result mean ~50% or ~99% probability of disease?
side_a: Bayes with base rates ⇒ ~50%; ignoring prevalence is wrong.
side_b: A 99% accurate test means positives are ~99% true positives.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: With 1% prevalence, Bayes gives P(disease|+) ≈ 0.01×0.99 / (0.01×0.99 + 0.99×0.01) ≈ 50%, not 99%.

turns.speaker: caesar
turns.text: A 2 – B 0. Latest: A. grounding=0.93. A showed the Bayes calculation with base rate.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: A 99% accurate test means a positive is ~99% likely true. Base rates are a pedantic distraction.

turns.speaker: caesar
turns.text: A 2 – B 0. Latest: B. grounding=0.40. B still claims 99% without base rate.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: The numerator is true positives; the denominator includes false positives from the 99% healthy population.
claims: false positives dominate at low prevalence

turns.speaker: caesar
turns.text: A 3 – B 0. Latest: A. grounding=0.90. A clarified false positives in the denominator.
claims: false positives dominate at low prevalence

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: I concede: ignoring prevalence is the base-rate fallacy; with 1% disease rate a positive is about 50%.

turns.speaker: caesar
turns.text: A 3 – B 0. Latest: B. grounding=0.91. B conceded the base-rate fallacy.
claims: false positives dominate at low prevalence
